# CC03: 蒨园 Qian Yuan

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC03` · Page: `/scenes/#CC03` · Row: `research/buildings/CC03-qian-yuan/`

## What it was

蒨园 Qian Yuan, west of 澹怀堂 among stream and rocks, with a west-facing gate, the three-bay 朗润斋, 湛景楼, 菱香沜, the rock 青莲朵 (brought from the old 德寿宫 at Hangzhou), 标胜亭, 别有天, 韵天琴, 委宛藏, and a stele pavilion holding the recut 梅石碑 (S05 j83:7a-8a; E0103, E0092). Begun 1752, eight scenes named in 1753 (E0091, E0104); its south-east was much rebuilt about 1808 with the five-bay 碧静堂 and four new scenes named by Jiaqing in 1809 (E0104, E0105), on an ink plan of 1808 (样067-1, E0106). The 1808 state, not the 1753 one, stood in 1860.

From the inventory row: **built** 乾隆十八年 1753 poems [j83:7b]; 1752; **changed** c. 1808 south-east rebuilt, 碧静堂; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S06, S01, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not in the Forty Scenes. Qianlong named eight views of 蒨园 in 1753 (朗润斋, 湛景楼, 菱香沜, 青莲朵, 别有天, 韵天琴, 标胜亭, 委宛藏; S05 j83:8a-9a, E0091, E0104); Jiaqing named four after the rebuilding, in 1809 (虚受轩, 委宛藏, 碧静堂, 菱香沜; E0104).
